items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: Thompson, Joe Newman and Russell Jacquet, and J. J. Johnson, Al Lucas on bass on -- Shadow Wilson on drum

ctx.x: And as I say, it was the first time I had seen Kenny since then, and during that time as I told you I did so many recordings with Jacquet Jacquet and Dizzy also. As a matter of fact one of them was "Muttin Leg" Mudden-Leg, with Illinois Jacquet Jacquet, and his orchestra. And in that band was Leo Parker and Sir Charles

Thompson, Joe Newman and Russell Jacquet, and J. J. Johnson, Al Lucas on bass on -- Shadow Wilson on drum, which was quite 'Ow' 'Oo Pop A Dum' a band. And I know that I did Owi and Ooh-Bopadomp, with Dizzy, yeah. And let's see, who was in this band. David Elman Burns, Simon Wright and Matthew McKay and Ray Orr was trumpet. Howard Johnson and John Brown, alto sax, and James Moore Moody and Joe Gales, tenor sax. Cecil Payne was in the band, baritone. And John Lewis, piano, Ray Brown, bass, Milt Jackson and Joe…

But you know, it's kind of difficult to remember all of the personnel because it's been so long, but during that era it was kind of nice in that I had been away in the army and when I came back I was thrown right back with the Beboppers. You know. So that was kind of gratifying to me, but I had done quite a bit of research and practicing because I was aware of what was happening, even though I was in the army. Because music had changed all together when I came -- it was strictly the swing era when I went in. When…
